facts.title: The Birthplace of Yerevan
facts.text: In 782 BC, King Argishti I founded Erebuni Fortress to secure his northern border.
The king settled 6,600 captives from Khate and Tsupani to build and populate this citadel.

facts.title: 24,100 kapis
facts.text: Granaries stored over 24,100 kapis of grain, alongside giant jars of wine and beer.

facts.title: The Temple of Khaldi
facts.text: This major sanctuary featured blue frescoes depicting deities, hunting scenes, and trees of life.

facts.title: Peaceful Evacuation
facts.text: Urartians peacefully evacuated Erebuni for Teishebaini, allowing exceptional preservation of the site.

facts.title: Carved in Basalt
facts.text: The discovery of the foundation inscription confirmed the site of the fortress that gave Yerevan its name.

facts.title: 2,750th
facts.text: In September 1968, the 2,750th anniversary of Erebuni formalized the venerable age of the capital.

ytTitle: Erebuni, the Ancient Urartian Fortress That Became Yerevan
ytLead: Founded in 782 BC by King Argishti I, Erebuni Fortress is the historical birthplace of the Armenian capital. Its basalt ramparts and royal frescoes bear witness to the power of the Urartian civilization.
